params.body:
A script used the newsletter form on gentells.com to send confirmation mails ("Confirm your subscription to Gen Tells This Week") to strangers through Resend, on the night of 10 to 11 November 2026. The form mails whatever address is typed into it, its only brake was a per-IP throttle, and an unconfirmed address got a new mail on every post.

Closes #273

## What changes

- **Cloudflare Turnstile** on the two public forms that send mail: newsletter (every place it appears, including the cover) and contact. `App\Http\Middleware\Turnstile` verifies the token with Cloudflare before the controller runs. A missing or rejected token is refused, with a plain line under the email field. Two cases let the form through: no keys configured (the check is off, so this can be deployed before the keys exist), and Cloudflare unreachable (an outage there must not cost a reader their message). The widget runs `interaction-only`, so almost nobody sees it.
- **One confirmation mail per address per day**, however often it is posted (`NewsletterSubscriber::sendConfirmation`, new column `confirmation_sent_at`). The link in the first mail keeps working. This holds even if something gets past Turnstile, and it stops anyone flooding a single inbox.
- CSP: `script-src` and `frame-src` allow `https://challenges.cloudflare.com`, only when Turnstile is configured.
- Privacy policy: Cloudflare listed as a processor for the bot check.

Same approach as the `SpamGuard` on hoet.be and cabrio-eyewear.be, without its honeypot and timer: a script that renders the page passes those, and Turnstile is the gate.

## To go live

1. Cloudflare dashboard > Turnstile > Add widget: hostname `gentells.com` (DNS does not have to be at Cloudflare), mode Managed.
2. Forge env for gentells.com: `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` and `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`.
3. Deploy, which runs the migration.

Until step 2 is done only the one-a-day rule is active.

## Tests

`NewsletterGuardTest`: works as before without keys; no token means no mail and no message; an accepted token goes through and the secret is sent to Cloudflare; a rejected token sends nothing; Cloudflare down lets the form through; five posts of one address give one mail, a second one after a day; the widget and CSP sources appear only with keys, one script for two forms. The full suite passes apart from BuildStampTest, which fails in any worktree.

Does not overlap with #272: it changes other lines in `contact.blade.php` and `privacy-en.md`, and does not touch `FormController`.

params.title: Turnstile on the forms that send mail, one confirmation a day per address
